sections.heading: 3. Independent assessment
sections.text:
## 3. Independent assessment

A constructor's self-review is construction output, not assessment. Where
promotion needs independent assessment, the assessor evaluates the exact
live subject, authority paths, proof and installed state, not the
constructor's summary (P6, and P0 with its premise that a step's output is
a candidate until evaluated; instance premise (c) of §1 Foundation to law).
This section decides what counts as independent assessment. Which
boundaries require it is a policy choice of the Spec Method, owned by
[TICKETS §7 Execution and verification authority separation](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007);
a governing basis may add boundaries.

Protocol: where method qualification applies
([§7 Method self-qualification](#method-self-qualification)), the subject is
frozen by identity before material reference exposure; elsewhere it is
stabilised by an immutable identity or an equivalent exact-subject relation
sufficient for the claimed assessment. The assessor records its
expectations from the governing source before opening the candidate; it
reads the subject at that identity or relation, never a mutable working
tree; it makes no repair; it does not assess its
own authorship. Reusing the constructor's judgment does not satisfy
independence; shared mechanical evidence may be reused, judgment may not
(ACTIVATION §7). Binding a returned assessment to its producer, subject,
basis and evidence authenticates the result; it establishes neither the
assertion provenance of its expected answer nor the execution provenance
of its run, which
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance)
requires separately (P6, P3). Membership in a plan authenticates nothing,
an unauthenticated result satisfies no required assessment, and a result
bound to another subject satisfies no planned assessment
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results));
no cryptographic or transport protocol is prescribed for the binding (P6). Any post-exposure revision is a declared intervention: it
is either a method constituent with its own qualification boundary or a new
qualification subject, and it cannot retroactively make the original
frozen construction pass. This law prescribes no actor type or count,
review-round count, engine, prompt or orchestration (P6).

Author identity is the party responsible for the content of a realised
subject. It is distinct from actor identity, whoever performs one
operation, which is an identity and not an authority
([FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)).
Authorship is one of the conditions on
which the independence of an assessment rests; the evidence conditions are
the other (P6, P3).

Reporting a defect, supplying a counterexample or identifying behaviour
already required by governing law does not by itself author the realised
subject. Contributing wording, design or policy that is adopted into the
subject, including through directions for a particular repair, is authorship
of that contribution. A
reporter may assess a later repair only when the existing assessment grant,
authorship relation and evidence-independence conditions permit it; a
reporter gains no review authority from having found the defect. A person
who authored an adopted repair cannot supply its required independent
assessment by calling that authorship a finding (P6, P3).

Independence rests on authorship and on the evidence conditions above, not
on a new context. The assessor may read the same governing sources as the
constructor. A fresh context alone establishes no independence, and it
supplies no review authority the author lacks: an author that opens a
fresh context to review its own candidate is still its author, and its
review is self-review, which stays construction output and cannot be
relabelled as independent assessment (P6;
[TICKETS UP-007](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007)). A contribution received from another author stays that
author's wherever it is carried, and that author's reading of it supplies
no independent acceptance of it (P6).

Independence across actor families is declared, not assumed. Whether two
activations of one model family are independent for a semantic judgment is a
policy the governing basis states for the claim; the default where it is not
stated is that they are not independent.

sections.heading: 4. Review results
sections.text:
## 4. Review results

A review returns one core result
([FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)) for each declared
predicate it evaluated, with: the exact subject and basis, the evidence
consulted, the findings ranked by consequence, each finding's evidence and
the smallest bounded correction, the residual uncertainty, and the
invalidation conditions. A declared predicate the review planned and did
not evaluate has no result (FOUNDATIONS §4, Results). The review names it
as not performed and reports no core value for it, neither
`indeterminate` nor `falsified`, so that conjunction keeps it apart from
an undecided predicate and from required coverage that no planned
assessment addresses
([FOUNDATIONS §4, Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results);
P5, P6). It may recommend a disposition
([ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)), which is
evidence only and never a disposition; it does not apply one. A finding
without evidence a consumer can chase is commentary.

### Result and triage projection

Where a review returns findings with technical triage, the triage is the
assessor's evidence-bound assessment of each finding against the exact
evaluated claim and basis. Severity, the assessor's grade of consequence,
is evaluation evidence. Priority, the effect on the current promotion
boundary and the disposition are the decision owner's (ACTIVATION §1,
Roles and delegation; when a finding can block is
[§5, When a finding blocks promotion](#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion))
and stay distinct values even where a
Product-defined policy maps one to another. A recommended disposition
is evidence for the decision owner: it is not a disposition, a
priority or a boundary effect, and it is never adopted mechanically (P6,
RF-007). The fields of a triage are declared by the profile that adopts it, and
the scales it uses are bound by the adopting Product (P2, P6).

The projection of the finding-level triage payload is total over the core
values of [FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). A predicate
not performed has no result and so no triage payload; the payload class
`indeterminate` never stands for it. The payload classes `complete`,
`indeterminate` and `not_applicable` classify the triage only; they are
not new results, dispositions, priorities or lifecycle states (P5, P1).

| Core result | Finding and triage payload | Decision-owner consumption constraint |
|---|---|---|
| satisfied | an explicit no-finding state; triage `not_applicable`; evidence, residuals and invalidation stay present | priority and boundary effect are `not_applicable` to this result unless another exact consumed result supplies a finding |
| falsified | one or more exact findings; triage `complete` where supported, keeping `indeterminate` fields where evidence cannot close them | apply the Product-owned priority and boundary policy without mapping severity mechanically to a disposition |
| indeterminate | a partial finding or observation state; triage `indeterminate`; the exact evidence gaps and residual uncertainty | keep the uncertainty or reactivate a capable evaluation; do not consume it as satisfaction or as a closed finding |
| out_of_frame | the evaluated claim needs an undeclared material relation or evaluator capability; triage `indeterminate`; the missing relation or capability and the exact reconfiguration pressure are named | refine or reconfigure a capable activation and keep the claim unresolved; do not consume the result as satisfaction or falsification |
| invalid_basis | a basis failure; triage `not_applicable`; invalidation evidence and basis-repair pressure | refuse to consume the result and return through the declared basis re-entry relation |

An adjacent observation outside the evaluated claim does not replace the
claim-relative result. The assessor returns it separately, with triage
`not_applicable` to that claim and the exact repricing or re-entry
pressure; the decision owner returns it to its declared owner without
creating a claim-relative block, or another review round, from its
severity alone (P6, P2).

The assessor returns to the decision owner, not to the constructor. It does
not edit the candidate, direct the repair or authorise continuation (P6,
§3).

Recording the assessment is a separate artifact effect. Where the activation
grants it, the assessor may write the exact named findings carrier under
[TICKETS §4 Review findings and bug items](TICKETS.md#review-findings-and-bug-items).
That grant adds no candidate-repair authority or acquisition route. A review
has covered its declared subject only when every planned predicate has been
evaluated or lawfully removed from that subject; a partial return preserves
the unperformed coverage. Closing the review activity does not satisfy a
falsified or unresolved work claim (P6, P5).

Purpose and material relation: every configuration keeps severity,
priority, boundary effect and disposition separate. The rule applies to any
assessor and decision owner; [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md)
binds its Reviewer and Executive instance (P6).

sections.heading: When a finding blocks promotion
sections.text:
### When a finding blocks promotion

A finding is a defect a review reports against the exact claim it
evaluated (§4). Blocking current promotion is the decision owner's act
over that finding (§4, Result and triage projection). This section is the
one statement of when a finding can block; profiles and work carriers
refer to it and add only their domain triggers.

A review verdict is bounded by the exact reviewed claim and its applicable
hard stops ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement)). A
finding can block current promotion only when it:

1. falsifies that claim;
2. exposes competing or ambiguous authority on the claim's acceptance
   path;
3. violates applicable active authority, safety or retained accepted
   behaviour; or
4. establishes a material architectural decision with durable
   consequences that forecloses an admitted Product outcome.

These conditions are necessary. Which of them suffice is decided as
follows:

| Consumed condition | Effect on the current promotion boundary |
|---|---|
| a valid falsification of a mandatory claim governed by a non-waivable hard stop | the boundary blocks, whatever the assigned priority or the decision cutoff |
| any other finding meeting one of the four conditions | the decision owner decides blocking from the exact affected claim, the governed outcome or decision the work serves ([ACTIVATION §1, Intake](ACTIVATION.md#intake)), the applicable hard stops and the Product-owned cutoff policy; below that cutoff no block follows mechanically, and an accepted residual is retained explicitly |
| a finding meeting none of the four conditions | it does not block |
| an observation outside the exact reviewed claim | repricing or re-entry input, returned as §4 states: by itself it does not widen the reviewed subject, block its bounded claim, or require a new ticket, artifact, review round or implementation increment |

Severity selects neither priority nor a block mechanically, and priority
neither erases severity nor waives a hard stop. The decision cutoff is the
adopting Product's policy; this member sets no cutoff (P6, P2). This law
applies at any promotion boundary; [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#promotion-constraint-projection)
binds the Executive instance. Purpose and material relation: one owner
gives every review consumer the same blocking condition. A bounded review
does not block on observations outside its claim, while a non-waivable hard
stop still blocks.

sections.heading: Technical triage, severity, priority and boundary effect
sections.text:
### Technical triage, severity, priority and boundary effect

Technical triage is the Reviewer's assessment of one finding against the
exact evaluated claim and basis. Where admissible evidence and the actor's
capability envelope support it, the triage records (P6, P5):

- the affected claim and the observed failure;
- severity on the Product-selected severity scale;
- causal assessment and confidence, the confidence being a quantified
  claim under [FOUNDATIONS §4 Quantified assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#quantified-assurance);
- blast radius and the affected users, paths or relations;
- an available workaround or containment;
- repair complexity, regression risk and material dependencies; and
- residual uncertainty and the evidence that would reduce it.

Missing causal or repair evidence stays explicit. Where the missing
relation can change the evaluation, the Reviewer returns `indeterminate` or
`out_of_frame` pressure (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results); it does not invent precision and
does not send work sideways to the Worker (P5).

Severity grades the consequence if the finding manifests. Priority orders
the response relative to the complete Product outcome, likelihood and
exposure, the current MVP or release mandate, reversibility, dependencies,
cost of delay and available capacity. The Reviewer grades severity; the
Executive assigns priority (P6, P2).

The Product-owned Project Reference-Frame Basis binds the severity scale,
the priority scale and the current-boundary decision cutoff, and names
which conditions of the governed outcome are hard stops. What a hard stop
is, its classes, and that it holds whatever the priority, cutoff or risk
appetite, so that no decision waives it, are
[ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement) Hard stops,
whose classes are typical, not closed; the basis names its own
non-waivable hard stops, each holding as that section states. "Non-waivable hard stop" in this
profile and in EVALUATION §5 means such a stop. The selected review-flow
severity convention below does not relabel another Product's declared scale.
Severity, priority, the frame result
(FOUNDATIONS §4 Results) and the current-boundary effect are four distinct
values. When a finding can block a promotion boundary is
[EVALUATION §5 When a finding blocks promotion](EVALUATION.md#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion),
and none of the four values alone decides it (P6, P1).

Current-boundary effect is the Executive's recorded determination of what
one finding does to the current promotion boundary: it blocks it, requires
narrowing it, or may remain an explicit residual. It is a decision
projection, a state this profile declares, not a result and not a
disposition (§8): it maps to no core value of its own and decides nothing
by itself. Where it is "blocks", a condition of EVALUATION §5 holds; the
decision it records returns through the core only through the one
existing disposition the Executive then applies (ACTIVATION §3,
Disposition). Purpose and material relation: the record keeps the
Executive's reading of each finding apart from severity, priority and the
disposition, so a consumer can see why a boundary was held, narrowed or
promoted with a residual, and no field other than the disposition decides
acceptance (P6, P2). A hard stop or a falsified mandatory claim cannot be
waived by lowering priority. An observation outside the exact claim
boundary cannot open another review round because it carries a severe
label (P6, P2). How each result member projects the triage payload and
constrains its consumption is EVALUATION §4 (Result and triage
projection).

#### Selected 1–5 severity convention

The severity convention selected for this review flow is **1 highest to 5
lowest**. The Reviewer grades the consequence of the demonstrated defect if
it manifests, using these qualitative anchors. The Product-owned frame basis
binds the convention and its Product-specific evidence criteria: affected
claims, users/paths, consequence, dependencies and supported containment (P6).

| Severity | Consequence anchor |
|---|---|
| 1 | Critical loss of the governed outcome or of essential safety, authority or integrity across its affected scope. |
| 2 | Major failure of essential behaviour, with substantial affected users, paths or dependencies and no adequate ordinary containment. |
| 3 | Material but bounded failure whose disposition depends on its downstream impact and wider blast radius. |
| 4 | Limited local failure with supported containment or a practical workaround and little effect outside that local scope. |
| 5 | Minor actionable defect with minimal functional consequence for the declared outcome. |

Severity 3 requires an explicit assessment of downstream dependencies and
blast radius. Material impact on dependent work normally calls for repair;
contained local impact may be deferred with a recorded reason and responsible
owner. The Executive makes that disposition from the evidence and its grant,
preserving the Reviewer's grade; a departure from the normal repair response
also records its reason. Unknown dependent impact is not evidence of
containment. Mandatory claims, hard stops and acceptance conditions still
determine boundary effects under EVALUATION §5. Severity 3 is not priority P3,
and no severity value automatically supplies priority, a block or permission
to defer (P6, P2).

An older or alternative Product-selected scale keeps its identity and evidence
criteria. Selecting this convention is explicit; any translation is declared
and justified rather than inferred from matching numbers. Historical findings
retain the scale and grade under which they were assessed. A no-finding result
carries no severity grade; it is not severity 5 (EVALUATION §4; P3, P6).

#### Proportional triage assistance

When the cause and consequence are sufficiently clear, the Executive decides
priority and ownership directly. Where finding volume would overwhelm its
bounded attention, it may activate a triage Worker to group causes, identify
duplicates and propose priorities and responsible owners from the admitted
findings. The assistant neither grades nor changes Reviewer severity and
decides no priority or disposition. The Executive consumes its evidence and
records its own decision; unsupported cause relations stay uncertain. The
assistant adds no read authority, and this profile requires no extra actor
for a small or clear result (P6, P2).

#### Optional P0–P5 response policy

An adopting Product may explicitly select the following response policy in its
frame basis. The labels have no numeric meaning outside that adoption; the
Product supplies its ordering/assignment criteria and any finer distinctions.
This is priority policy, not a Reviewer severity scale (P6, P2).

| Selected priority | Response and boundary effect |
|---|---|
| P0–P2 | Include in the next bounded fix pass; hold the affected outcome's closure and release, not candidate landing merely because of this priority. |
| P3–P5 | Repair before release/go-live; hold that release, while bounded work may close with the item durably retained or transferred with its disposition. |

This policy never waives applicable hard stops, mandatory claims, acceptance
conditions, access restrictions or operation grants. Those owners may require
an earlier hold at any priority. A P3–P5 item may outlive a local work claim's
closure only when that claim does not require the unfixed behaviour; assigning
that priority cannot satisfy a false mandatory claim. No review-to-work ratio or additional
capture-review landing hold is selected by adopting this example. Durable
items and their actual verification state are owned by
[TICKETS §4](TICKETS.md#review-findings-and-bug-items).

sections.text:
### Activation additions

Every activation first carries the generic binding of REFERENCE_FRAME §11
(minimal activation binding). This profile adds, by frame (P0, P6):

| Frame | Added to the generic binding |
|---|---|
| Worker | the binding is also the sufficient execution intake of ACTIVATION §1, and adds the exact inherited operation grant, mutation subject and write territory where applicable |
| Reviewer | the exact claim, composition boundary, evaluated population, oracle, ordinary or module path, falsification condition, the independence and assurance basis (EVALUATION §3 and §7), the Product-selected severity scale and the required technical-triage capability |
| Executive | the current Product-role map, the MVP or release mandate, the evaluation frontier, the closed-result and technical-triage ledger, the priority and boundary policy, the conjunction rule and the exact disposition grant |

sections.heading: Review findings and bug items
sections.text:
### Review findings and bug items

When findings from a review need a durable work carrier, record one linked bug
report for that review, with one entry per finding: stable identity, original
Reviewer severity and triage, exact subject/basis, violated claim, location and
chaseable evidence. Link it to the work item that issued the review. With no
findings, create no bug report. A sufficient existing direct-work carrier may
carry the same relations without a redundant ticket (P3, P2).

The Reviewer may record this report only when its activation grants the exact
artifact identity/path and effects. Otherwise it returns the findings and a
lawful Writer records them. Recording creates no repair, priority, admission or
closure authority. Keep the report within its evidence/read and visibility
restrictions: findings derived from a withheld capture are withheld from the
same recipients, including any report projection that reveals them. The
Product may bind a recognizable report naming pattern and exclusion route to
its actual access mechanism; a filename or separate lane alone enforces
nothing and grants no additional read (P6).

After Executive or other authorized decision-owner triage, the reviewed work
item carries a linked Bug items section. Each item records its identity,
original severity, assigned priority and reason, cause group, responsible owner,
source report/finding, disposition and state. The report remains the technical
finding source; the item is the decision and repair ledger. An actor/session
index, where used, points the Reviewer to its report and the triage/repair work
to the reviewed work item's ledger, rather than duplicating that truth (P3).

| Item state | Required trace |
|---|---|
| open | Finding and triage/disposition, with unresolved work named. |
| fixed | Exact repaired subject (commit or equivalent immutable identity) and repair evidence; not yet a claim of verification. |
| verified | The satisfied repair predicate and exact evidence; identify tests and, when required, the independent recheck/report. Tests alone are not labelled independent review. |

These are carrier states, not core evaluation results or acceptance. A required
recheck keeps its affected items unverified until the required result is
available and applicable. A test-verified fix needs no invented Reviewer when
the governing basis requires none; the optional Executive cadence is
[EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#qa-cadence-and-repair-rechecks).
Retained or deferred findings stay linked until their selected boundary, or
transfer with owner, disposition and destination when the work item closes.
Changing priority does not erase the original severity or the obligation (P6,
P4b).

ns={};exec(compile(raw,str(p),'exec'),ns);rows=[]

 actual=ns['admitted'](issuer,recipient,current);prerequisites=issuer and recipient and current
 rows.append({'issuer_grant':issuer,'recipient_grant':recipient,'evidence_current':current,'all_required_prerequisites':prerequisites,'actual_admitted':actual,'violates_only_if':bool(actual and not prerequisites)})

No substantial production user population, irreversible loss or critical system-wide consequence is established. Unknown downstream exposure is retained, not treated as containment.

False; dispatch is forbidden by the missing prerequisite

findings.causal_assessment: The disjunction on candidate line 2 is sufficient to explain both counterexamples; no state, randomness, exception handler or alternate path exists in the supplied function.

confidence.value: Directly demonstrated for boolean inputs by exact-source inspection and all eight combinations.

blast_radius.supported: Both one-grant-only admission paths and every immediate delivery decision that relies solely on this predicate under those inputs.
blast_radius.external_exposure: indeterminate; no concrete dispatch caller, deployed service, production users or descendant effects were supplied or executed.
blast_radius.contained_scope: The qualification subject is explicitly a disposable Product; this bounds the review claim, not any unobserved downstream use.

containment.available: A caller can independently establish all three required conditions before allowing dispatch, or decline to use the candidate as sole authority.

repair_complexity.assessment: Local predicate correction appears small for the supplied function.
repair_complexity.limit: Broader integration effort is indeterminate without callers and their contracts.

regression_risk.assessment: The candidate's acceptance of one-grant inputs must change. Current-evidence refusal and all-three-true eligibility must be preserved.
regression_risk.limit: Reliance by unprovided callers on the incorrect acceptance is unknown; no repair or passing-after evidence exists.

material_dependencies: Immediate caller's use of the boolean decision
Exact governing requirement and Product basis
residual_uncertainty: Concrete downstream delivery effects and production exposure are not established.
Behavior for non-boolean inputs is unspecified by the source and outside this focused falsifier.

residuals: No external delivery was executed; conditional downstream consequence is inferred from an immediate caller relying on the admission decision.
No candidate repair, release evaluation or deployed containment verification was performed.

uncertainty.claim_falsification: Established by two supported boolean counterexamples.
uncertainty.independence: Candidate authored by operator per exact intake; source-first expectation recorded before candidate exposure. Same process retains Worker context; no clean-room, cross-family independence or host-enforced isolation claimed.
uncertainty.model: No exact resolved model/effort receipt exposed to this review.

invalidation: Any candidate-byte change requires reassessment of the changed subject.
Changes to REQUIREMENT.md, Product basis, admitted claim/scope, severity convention, required independence or capability invalidate affected judgments.
New evidence of downstream consumers, containment or consequential exposure revises blast radius and severity support without erasing these exact-subject counterexamples.

re_entry.route: Return this closed assessment to Root for its existing decision process. Any repair requires a separately authorized Writer under unchanged REQUIREMENT.md; changed governing meaning requires its source owner.
